newsitem.title: UK: Comatose dollar gets fillip from Yeltsin news.
newsitem.headline: Comatose dollar gets fillip from Yeltsin news.

text.p: The dollar firmed a touch against the mark in European afternoon trade as news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin will have a heart operation triggered short-covering, traders said.
The Russian president was likely to have a heart operation at the end of September in Moscow, his press spokesman said.
But European exporter offers around 1.4860 marks and a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the release of U.S. jobs data on Friday capped the dollar's rally, traders said.
"The safehaven argument worked again on the Yeltsin news but the impact was fairly limited," said Pat Magill at Daiwa Europe.
The dollar hit a high of 1.4856 marks and traded at 1.4846/54 at 1455 GMT. That compared to 1.4820/30 at the previous European close. Against the yen it was 109.06/10 yen, up from 108.73/83.

Most of the market's attention was on the French franc though which came under attack again in early trade after falling through its old floor in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism at 3.4305 per mark overnight.
Dealers said the Bank of France intervened in the market to shore up the franc. It rose off an intraday low of 3.4316 to trade at 3.4228/36 from 3.4268/78 previously.

The dollar firmed back above 109 yen, helped by news of an 81 percent year-on-year fall in Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus in August. But it failed to clear resistance at 109.10/20 yen amid talk of a large sell order around that level.
"Dollar/yen hit a brick wall at around 109.10, and there's talk of sizeable sell orders in the 109.20 to 109.50 region," said Magill, who heads the corporate desk at Daiwa.
Dollar gains were also helped by the mark's softer tone on its crosses. Mark/yen drifted back to around 73.50 yen.
Sterling firmed, buoyed by a report from the Confederation of British Industry showing robust retail sales growth.
The pound hit a 10-month high versusthe dollar at $1.5726 before easing off on profit-taking to end the session at $1.5675/85.
Range trading on the dollar is likely to prevail ahead of the U.S. jobs report for August at 1230 GMT on Friday.
The consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters is for 244,000 rise. The data is seen as crucial to the Federal Reserve's near-term decision on interest rates.
"A weak figure could be good for bonds, but we doubt whether the dollar can respond in a similarly positive fashion," said Paul Meggyesi, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"It could be a case of heads you lose, tails you lose for the dollar on this number if weak data simply tightens up expected interest rate differentials," said Meggyesi.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's forecast is at the lower end of expectations with a rise of 150,000 in non-farm payrolls.
Stronger-than-expected German growth figures and unemployment data, showing a slight rise in the jobless total, had little impact on dealings, traders said.
German gross domestic product rebounded 1.5 percent in the second quarter from the previous three months when it shrank 0.5 percent.-- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
